mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 4.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction permits (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in demand, triggering a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of supply chain bottlenecks characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100 and falling for two months), corporate input costs rise and margins compress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO is below 100 and declining for two consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer spending (RSAFS) exceeds its 12-month high by 5%, it indicates strong demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month high by 5%, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a broad-based economic slowdown in manufacturing and construction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both INDPRO and HOUST decline for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL above 3.0% annually), the central bank maintains restrictive monetary policy, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above 3.0% annually, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.
